findings.reason: the plan should say whether it extends analyze_units with an unknown-unit verdict or deliberately forks the pint test, so the unit logic has one owner rather than two.
findings.text: §4's unit filter ("uses the dimension check behind analyze_units"; "drops a candidate only when both units are known and their dimensions differ") needs a dimensionality comparison that analyze_units computes internally (q_sig.dimensionality == q_imas.dimensionality) but does not expose: analyze_units returns only a `compatible` bool, and returns compatible=False when either unit is unknown, so it cannot be called as-is to get §4's keep-if-unknown semantics; candidates.py will therefore fork the pint comparison rather than extend its owner.

findings.reason: §8 must either guard both MATCH-gated writers or state why graph_ops.py:357 is deliberately out of scope, and the plan should name the single owner of signal→IMAS edge writes so §6's write_candidates and §8's persist are co-located rather than split across two modules.
findings.text: MAPS_TO_IMAS is written by two owners: imas_codex/ids/models.py:580 (the persist path §8 guards) and imas_codex/ids/graph_ops.py:357 in create_signal_source, which writes through the same `MATCH (ip:IMASNode {id: m.target_path})` + MERGE, so a target path naming no node drops the edge silently — the exact silent-drop §8 exists to close; §8 adds the returned-count guard only to models.py, leaving its goal "A binding can no longer vanish silently" unmet for the graph_ops writer, and §1 names models.py as the MAPS_TO_IMAS writer while §6 adds write_candidates to graph_ops.py without naming that module as a signal→IMAS edge owner. The two writers are the complete census of MAPS_TO_IMAS write sites in imas_codex/ids/ (models.py:580, graph_ops.py:357).
